extracted.intended_audience: offshore renewable energy developers, OCS lessees/grant holders, bidders, and industry stakeholders (and their counsel/consultants)
extracted.subtask_description: Section-by-section preamble and proposed regulatory text for BOEM's revisions to 30 CFR part 585 governing renewable energy on the Outer Continental Shelf, describing requirements for safety management systems, inspections, leases, auctions, definitions, reporting, and related procedures. Intended to solicit public comment and explain BOEM expectations and implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Management System (SMS) expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposes a performance-based approach clarifying expectations of the SMS for the regulated community; lessees or grant holders are expected to design, implement, and maintain the SMS according to widely accepted standard practices and may adopt U.S. and international workplace health and safety standards as the SMS framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon SMS receipt, the Department would engage with the lessee or grant holder to understand the risks the safety system was designed to mitigate and how the system would function. The proposed rule provides transparency regarding types of information considered necessary in a satisfactory SMS and clarifies that an SMS performance-based approach to risk management establishes a reasonable regulatory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive for SMS certification by recognized CAB
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would provide incentives for a lessee or grant holder to obtain certification of its SMS from a recognized safety and environmental management system certification/ accreditation body (CAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lessee or grant holder whose SMS has been certified would be eligible for streamlined oversight in recognition of increased rigor. Such certifications would not be required and cannot guarantee streamlined oversight in all instances, but BOEM anticipates most would pursue certification as a best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMS annual performance report (normalized)
rubrics_metrics.description: One reporting requirement: an annual summary of how the SMS performed, normalized to work hours and energy generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This report would allow the Department to verify SMS functionality, track continual improvements, and could be used to generate annual industry-wide comparisons of safety performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMS triannual audit report
rubrics_metrics.description: A triannual report summarizing results of the most recent SMS audit, corrective actions implemented, and a description of any changes made to the SMS since the prior report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data from these reports could be used to generate annual industry-wide comparisons of safety performance and to assess corrective action effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: functional SMS before any OCS activity and use for all activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee must have a functional SMS before beginning any activity on the OCS pursuant to a lease, and must use its SMS for all such activities, including site assessment work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies the stages at which an SMS must be functional and used, including prior to the SAP, COP, or GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessee-conducted annual onsite self-inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a facility has commenced commercial operations, the lessee would conduct an onsite inspection of its facility at least annually, including all safety equipment designed to prevent or ameliorate fires, spillages, or other major accidents, to satisfy the annual onsite inspection requirement of the OCS Lands Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lessee must maintain records of its self-inspections, summarize the results of those inspections, and provide the records and the summary to BOEM upon request. This makes the lessee accountable and allows scheduling efficiency by incorporating inspections into other onsite activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM inspection authority (may conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to BOEM's requirement “to conduct” an inspection to state that BOEM “may conduct” an inspection on an OCS facility or any vessel engaged in renewable activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department would retain the ability to conduct inspections at any time, including scheduled and unscheduled inspections; changing 'will'/'to conduct' to 'may conduct' reflects flexibility while retaining authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection prioritization / selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: DOI may focus resources on conducting inspections based on designated criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated criteria include operational risk severity and risk probability, industry trends, incident data, analytical data, safety management system implementation and audits, and other observations. This allows DOI to target inspections by higher risk or information-driven priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease term and structure changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes to default lease terms by merging preliminary and site assessment terms into one preliminary period; establishing new lease periods for COP review and design/construction that can vary in length; converting existing 25-year operations term that commences at COP approval into a 30-year operations period commencing at commercial operations date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes recognize most lessees will not submit SAPs, account for permit review and construction time, and provide certainty regarding the operations period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease segregation and consolidation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule would clarify existing regulations by establishing specific procedures to segregate a single lease into multiple leases or consolidate multiple adjacent leases into a single lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responds to lessee requests and codifies specific procedures; primarily a clarification rather than substantively new policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalties authority consistent with statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend regulations to ensure civil penalty provisions are coextensive with OCS Lands Act authority, including assessing immediate civil penalties for violations that constitute a threat of serious, irreparable, or immediate harm or damage without notice and opportunity to correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly reflect statutory authority to assess immediate penalties where such harm is present; aligns regulatory text with the OCS Lands Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized annual rental rate for grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed standardization of the annual rental rate for most grants to $5 per acre for both ROWs and RUEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to standardize and simplify annual rental assessments across grant types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of paper copy submission requirement (electronic submissions primary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule would eliminate the paper copy submission requirement for plans, applications, reports, and notices and rely primarily on electronic submissions; BOEM may reserve authority to require paper copies for certain documents (e.g., maps and charts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernizes procedures, reduces burden for voluminous plan submittals and multiple revisions, and removes the need to update mailing addresses in regulation text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory departures criteria (§585.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may prescribe or approve a departure from the regulations when BOEM deems the departure necessary because the applicable provision(s) as applied to a specific circumstance are impractical or unduly burdensome and the departure is necessary to achieve the intended objectives of the renewable energy program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departure must still be consistent with subsection 8(p), protect the environment and public health and safety, not impair third-party rights, and be documented in writing. Proposed change extends ability to apply departures to activities before lease issuance and after lease termination where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification that site assessment activities do not require a lease
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision to clarify that site assessment activities are not considered to produce, transport, or support the generation of any energy products and therefore such activities do not, by themselves, require a lease, easement or ROW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates deployment of met buoys or towers for site assessment not located on an existing commercial lease. USACE would be lead Federal permitting agency for such facilities, but other agencies (e.g., NOAA under NMSA) may have permitting or consultation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthened compliance responsibilities (§585.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modification to strengthen the requirement for lessees to comply with all applicable laws, regulations, other requirements, the terms of the lease or grant under this part, reports, notices, approved plans, and any conditions imposed by BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands and clarifies current language that was previously narrower; makes obligations explicit and broader in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification and disqualification criteria to acquire/hold leases (§585.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical and substantive changes: replace 'hold' with 'acquire or hold'; correct citizenship qualification language to be disjunctive; add criteria that may disqualify a party from acquiring a lease or grant interest (including certain misconduct); prohibit disqualified parties from participating via third parties; clarify BOEM's authority to disqualify from auctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party under consideration for disqualification would receive written notice, an opportunity to be heard, and BOEM may specify remedial actions to restore qualification. Until remedied, party is ineligible to acquire or participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: bidding credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidding credits are defined as the value assigned by BOEM, expressed in monetary terms, to the factors or actions demonstrated, or committed to, by a bidder at a BOEM lease auction during the competitive lease award process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FSN will set the types and values of bidding credits for a given auction; bidding credits may be used to incentivize policy goals and can be stackable or non-stackable depending on FSN provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify definitions for commercial activities and commercial operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify definitions so commercial activities are conducted 'under' leases and grants, and commercial operations means generation of electricity or other energy product for commercial use, sale, and distribution on a commercial lease, excluding generation needed only to prepare a final FIR or for testing (if not sold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns definitions with §585.104 and avoids requiring leases for purely site-assessment/test generation that is not commercial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Critical Safety System
rubrics_metrics.description: Add definition for 'Critical Safety System' to mean safety systems and equipment designed to prevent or ameliorate major accidents that could result in harm to health, safety, or the environment associated with the lessee's or grant holder's facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition clarifies new requirements in several sections for the CVA to verify the commissioning of critical safety systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: engineered foundation and fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineered foundation: any structure installed on the seabed using a fixed-bottom foundation constructed according to a professional engineering design (based on assessment of sedimentary, meteorological, or oceanographic conditions). Fabrication: the cutting, fitting, welding, or other assembly of project elements of a custom design conforming to project-specific requirements; does not include procurement of standardized, commercially available parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM solicits comments on appropriateness of the 'engineered foundation' definition; definitions clarify applicability of regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: receipt of a document
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'receipt' as deemed to take place, absent documentation to the contrary, (a) 5-business days after the document was given to a mail or delivery service with the proper address and postage; or (b) on the date the document was sent electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borrowed from IBLA regulation; presumption of constructive receipt can be overcome by evidence demonstrating actual receipt occurred earlier or later. Applies where timing of receipt triggers regulatory time periods or consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSN and FSN contents and separation; auction-related information
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify scope and separation of the Proposed Sale Notice (PSN) and Final Sale Notice (FSN): PSN proposes procedures and invites comment; FSN establishes final procedures and provisions. These notices are primary sources for prospective bidders on lease areas, auction procedures, and lease provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.223 would outline supplemental auction information that may be in PSN/FSN. The FSN may set a maximum number of lease areas an individual party may bid on or acquire in an auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area identification factors
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM would consider any factors it determines relevant during area identification, including but not limited to other uses in and around the area, applicable environmental analysis, formal and informal stakeholder comments, industry nominations, and the area's feasibility for development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility considerations could include area size and physical conditions, potential electrical generation capacity, technical data, and electricity market/offtake information; BOEM may consider bathymetry, distance to shore, wind resources, and adjacent State's offshore wind energy offtake or incentive programs. Area identification informs NEPA and interagency consultations; BOEM may develop lease stipulations, mitigation, and hold public hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding credits awarding and application process
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.216 allows the provisional winner's bid to include the value of bidding credits awarded if the provisional winner has made demonstrable commitments that facilitate OCS renewable energy development or advance public policy (e.g., a power purchase agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PSN/FSN will prescribe use of bidding credits for a particular auction including eligibility, application procedures, and types/values. A bidder must timely submit a bidding credit application and meet eligibility to be awarded credits before the auction. BOEM retains discretion not to offer bidding credits; in multiple factor auctions BOEM would add monetary value of bidding credits to cash bids to determine highest bidder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewable energy leasing schedule frequency and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a subpart defining a leasing schedule: at least once every 2 years, the Secretary would publish a schedule of proposed lease sales covering a 5-year period (first schedule for 5 years following effective date; subsequent schedules cover next 5-year period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule would include general description of area, calendar year of sale, and reasons for changes from previous schedule. Any proposed leasing remains subject to applicable regulations, area identification, coordination, and environmental reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and timing consolidation (§585.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine appeal provisions (previously in §§585.118 and 585.225) into a consolidated §585.118: characterize challenges to provisional winner selections as appeals to the Director, provide appeal rights to adversely affected bidders and provisional winners, and specify procedures and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM must receive written appeals of a decision selecting the provisional winner within 15 business days after notice; adopt rules in 30 CFR 590.3 for determining receipt. Provisional winners have opportunity to be heard before reversal; Director's decision would not be administratively appealable to the Interior Board of Land Appeals.
